raw_response:
I have been working this land for ten years now, and Quzhou's climate is what I know. The wheat-maize rotation is what my parents did and what my neighbors do — it makes sense for our land and our well water. I split my 18 mu so that 10 mu stays in rotation and the remaining 8 mu goes to my vegetables and stevia, which bring better cash than grain alone.

For wheat, I plant the improved Jimai variety — it yields well and the seed station in town always has it. I flood irrigate four times: before winter dormancy, the reviving water in March, jointing stage, and grain filling. My husband handles the tractor for rotary tillage after maize harvest each year.

For maize I go straight to hybrid seed — Zhengdan 958 mostly — because the yield jump is worth the cost. After wheat harvest I plant with minimal tillage to save time. Two or three irrigations is enough if the summer rains cooperate.

My cabbage plot in autumn is reliable money. I apply more pesticides there because the aphids and caterpillars are bad every year. Eggplant needs the most water and attention, so I keep it to 2 mu — I cannot manage more without help. Stevia I started three years ago when a company set up a purchase contract nearby; it is lower maintenance than vegetables and the buyer comes to collect.

I keep my fertilizer amounts close to what the township agronomist posted on the village board last year. I cannot read the technical sheet fully but I know the numbers from memory now.
